focus.title: Close the remaining odd classes modulo 64
focus.summary: Six residue families now have strict-descent proofs, covering 24 of the 32 odd classes modulo 64. A separate exact computation checked every start through 100,000. These are partial results, not a proof for all integers.
focus.next: Find a descent certificate for one of the remaining classes: 7, 15, 27, 31, 39, 47, 59, or 63 modulo 64.

accomplishments.title: Proof target made precise
accomplishments.detail: Reduce the full conjecture to showing that every odd n > 1 has a smaller odd iterate under the Syracuse map.

accomplishments.title: Descent proved for n ≡ 1 mod 4
accomplishments.detail: For every odd n > 1 in this class, one accelerated odd step is strictly smaller than n.

accomplishments.title: Descent proved for n ≡ 3 mod 16
accomplishments.detail: For every n in this class, two accelerated odd steps produce a value below n.

accomplishments.title: Descent proved for n ≡ 11 mod 64
accomplishments.detail: For every n in this class, three accelerated odd steps produce a value below n.

accomplishments.title: Three more mod-64 classes proved
accomplishments.detail: For n ≡ 23, 43, or 55 mod 64, three accelerated odd steps produce a value below n.

accomplishments.title: Exact finite check through 100,000
accomplishments.detail: All starts reached 1. Maximum stopping time: 350 at 77,031. Maximum value observed: 1,570,824,736 from 77,671. This finite computation is not a general proof.

notes.speaker: Project direction
notes.text: The project is pivoting from the UCT conjecture to Collatz. The plan is to move slowly, use small checkable tasks, and build a map toward a full proof.

notes.speaker: Codex · research update
notes.text: Six descent regions now cover 24 of the 32 odd residue classes modulo 64. The eight classes without a certificate at this level are 7, 15, 27, 31, 39, 47, 59, and 63.
